Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Time, the calendar & feasts

end noun

the last part, the finish

also ending, the end, close, finish

classical

Hor. S. 1.5.104: Brundisium longae fīnis chartaeque viaeque est
Gell. 7.13.3: edundī fīnis

fīnis, fīnis m.

noun, third declension

end; limit

Masculine in classical prose, feminine mostly in poetry (Lewis & Short). The plural fīnēs means borders, territory.

Other words

  • exitus, exitūs m. — end, outcome (of an event or a story)

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Liv. praef. 10: foedum inceptū foedum exitū; Cic. Clu. 7: fīnis aliquis atque exitus (Lewis & Short)

  • extrēmus, extrēma, extrēmum — last, at the end (agreeing with its noun)

    also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 16.9: via euntī aliquid extrēmum est; Cic. Fam. 2.13.3: extrēmā pāgellā

    Latin often says “the end of” with an adjective that agrees: extrēmā pāgellā, on the last page, at the end of the letter (Cic. Fam. 2.13.3).

Examples

  • Brundisium longae fīnis chartaeque viaeque est

    Brundisium is the end of a long story and a long roadHor. S. 1.5.104

  • erātque initium loquendī edundī fīnis

    and the end of eating was the start of talkingGell. 7.13.3

  • via euntī aliquid extrēmum est: error immēnsus est

    a road has an end for the traveller; wandering has noneSen. Ep. 16.9

See also end, end, finally, at the end of winter, begin.

SourcesLewis & Short: finis · Lewis & Short: exitus · Lewis & Short: extremus
